text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opinion polls reveal that supporters of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party are split on the issue of relations with Islamic sects.
- National Security Council warns against Kurdish separatist press and broadcasting and asks for decisiveness on Cyprus.
- Deputies from the conservative wing in the government are angered by Welfare's recent Islamist statements.
- Police in Ankara beat five people until they were unconscious because they drank alcohol in the holy fasting month of Ramadan.
- State-owned lands will be handed over to municipalities in order to halt unlicensed construction on them.
- German foreign minister did not apologise -- as his Turkish counterpart claimed -- for a statement by a German judge alleging Turkish government's support for international drug traffic.
- Turkey can be a base for the textile companies which are abandoning Hong Kong ahead of its hand over to Chinese rule.
- Chief of organised crime squad says Turkey seized 40 percent of all heroin intercepted worldwide last year.
